description: For a second-language learner, treating errors according to the activity's objective (accuracy or meaning), the learner's competence with the form, their affect and whether earlier corrections have taken hold is expected to improve accuracy at immediate and delayed tests better than one uniform correction policy; no claim in the wiki tests that matching, though corrective feedback as a whole has a durable effect and correction forms differ.
title: Employ flexible error treatment strategies matched to objectives, competence, affect, and correction effectiveness

description: In a class whose learners differ on the current task, forming temporary similar-need and mixed groups for a stated purpose from recent task evidence, and re-forming them as the evidence changes, is expected to match support and challenge to need better than one whole-class format, and to keep what targeted support gains without the costs fixed attainment sorting shows on grades, pass rates and the lowest group's classroom climate; no claim here tests flexible grouping itself, and the fixed-sorting evidence (one district's algebra policy) shows test-score gains for high attainers as well as those costs.
title: Flexible Grouping

description: For learners who can follow a topic's first explanation on their own, moving that first exposure before the live session and spending the freed time on application with feedback is expected to give better course outcomes than spending live time on the same exposition, provided learners prepare and the home time is not simply added; one meta-analysis of undergraduate health-professions courses found flipped classes ahead of lecture-based ones on exam performance (SMD 0.57), at low certainty with very high heterogeneity, and no claim here tests it with home time held equal.
title: Flipped Learning
